WHAT WE DO

∙ Learn practical engineering skills and applications beyond the classroom

∙ Network with professionals and other ASCE student chapters

∙ Access internships, job listings, and scholarships through ASCE Career Connections

∙ Prepare for the FE Exam with student member discounts

∙ Compete in regional and national ASCE events

∙ Get involved in community service and technical projects

WHY JOIN

∙ Build your resume and develop career-ready experience

∙ Connect with upperclassmen and professionals who've been where you are

∙ Get early access to job and internship opportunities

∙ Learn about different paths within civil engineering—from structures to transportation to water resources

∙ Be part of a community that supports your growth, both academically and professionally

DM us on Instagram @asce_fsc or email one of our officers!

name: Biology Club
summary: The biology club provides students with an interest in the biological sciences a community to engage with. Our club hosts events, talks, and trips to help members gain experience/knowledge within the different subfields of biology.
description: The purpose of the Biology Club is to provide Bioscience majors, as well as those with an interest in Biology, a place to make new friends and apply laboratory skills to fun projects. Our club aims to provide a welcoming and safe environment for all who share an interest in biology. Rather than focusing on one particular field of biology, the Biology Club will incorporate a diverse range of specializations within biology that will cater to the interests of students and faculty. To achieve this, we aim to host faculty guided events and field trips that focus on marine biology, medicine, ecology, evolution, microbiology, etc… Through these events we hope to introduce members to the diverse fields found within biology, and help members gain insight into fields they may not have otherwise become familiarized with. Given that the Biology Club relies on faculty participation, we also aim to help members make connections with faculty and potentially help facilitate student-mentor relationships. In addition to this, we aim to provide students with peer mentor guidance which is specific to those wishing to pursue a career in biology or other related fields. The Biology Club will share any relevant internship/research opportunities available. The Biology Club will also hold weekly general body meetings where future events will be announced and members can hang out, study, or discuss what they want to see in the club’s future.

summary: Campus Recreation engages the Farmingdale State College community in co-curricular experiences to inspire lifelong health and well-being. Participating in Campus Recreation is a great way to relieve stress, stay in shape, meet other students and continue
description:
Participating in Campus Recreation is a great way to relieve stress, stay in shape, meet other students and continue to play the sports that you love. Campus Recreation includes club sports, fitness and group exercise classes, intramurals, and more!

Club Sports are athletic based student organizations, which compete with other universities and colleges.

Our classes are drop-in fitness classes taught by certified instructors and designed for participants of all levels. Classes are FREE for Farmingdale students and staff with a valid Farmingdale ID Card. The expert coaching staff at AMP will take you through a balanced full-body strength training plan designed to help you feel stronger! We will use resistance to build muscle, shed fat, and burn calories. Never strength trained before? Don’t worry, we will make sure the workout is modified to accommodate all fitness levels. Let’s get stronger!

Intramural Sports are organized sports leagues, one-day tournaments, special events, and online programs, which provide participants the opportunity to compete against and engage with their fellow students and university community. Popular offerings include: basketball, dodgeball, flag football, soccer, softball, indoor and outdoor sand volleyball, and more!

name: Economics Society
summary: The Economics Society is a place where markets meet real life, blending finance, politics, history, and human behavior. Not just numbers and graphs; it is about understanding how the world actually works.
description: Economics is the study of how people, societies, and systems make choices in a world of limited resources, and those choices shape everything from the price of coffee to global power dynamics. It sits at the crossroads of money, psychology, politics, technology, and culture, revealing the hidden forces behind everyday decisions and major world events. Whether you are curious about why markets rise and fall, how policies affect real people, or how incentives quietly guide behavior, economics offers a way to see the world with sharper clarity. It is less about memorizing formulas and more about learning how to think, question assumptions, and understand the stories behind the data.

name: Farmingdale Student Investment Club
summary: The Student Investment Club is dedicated to enhancing financial literacy and investment knowledge. We offer a range of activities, including educational workshops, guest speaker events, stock market simulations and field trips!
description:
Welcome to the Farmingdale State College Student Investment Club! Our club is dedicated to empowering students with the knowledge and skills to navigate the world of finance and investing. Whether you're a seasoned investor or just starting out, our club offers a supportive and engaging environment for all.

What We Do:

- Educational Workshops: Gain insights into financial markets, investment strategies, and personal finance through our interactive workshops. Learn the basics of stocks, bonds, mutual funds, and other investment vehicles.

- Guest Speaker Events: Hear from industry professionals, alumni, and successful investors who share their experiences and provide valuable advice on how to succeed in the world of finance.

- Stock Market Simulations: Put theory into practice with our simulated trading sessions, where you can test your investment strategies in a risk-free environment.

- Portfolio Management Competitions: Compete with fellow members to create and manage the most successful investment portfolio. Prizes are awarded to top performers, adding an element of excitement and challenge.

- Networking Opportunities: Connect with peers, faculty, and industry professionals through our networking events. Build relationships that can help you in your academic and professional journey.

- Field Trips and Company Visits: Gain real-world exposure by visiting financial institutions, investment firms, and stock exchanges. See firsthand how the financial industry operates and explore potential career paths.

- Social Events: Join us for social gatherings, where you can relax, discuss the latest market trends, and build lasting friendships with fellow club members.

Whether you're looking to enhance your financial literacy, prepare for a career in finance, or simply explore the world of investing, the Farmingdale State College Investment Club has something to offer you. Join us today and start your journey towards financial empowerment!

name: Fraternities and Sororities
summary: Farmingdale State College currently has three nationally recognized sororities and four nationally recognized fraternities who are all guided by the Greek Council.
description:
Since the inception of FSC's first Greek organization in 2011, our fraternity and sorority system has rapidly grown over just a few years. We currently have three nationally recognized sororities and four nationally recognized fraternities who are all guided by the Greek Council.

On a daily basis, these organizations strive to uphold the four pillars of fraternity and sorority life: scholarship, leadership, philanthropy, and brotherhood/sisterhood. This tight-knit community of approximately 400 members has developed school traditions, promoted unity and inclusion, exceeded academic expectations, cultivated lifelong friendships, and created a high sense of school pride and community.

There are many career paths out there in the world, some are known and others unseen. Our mission is to promote and spread awareness of Medical Laboratory Science as a career option. When you go to the doctor's for a test and they take a sample from you. Where does it go? Well, we are the people who receive the sample, run the test, and give the result to the doctor, who finally gives the results to you, the patient.

Come join us in this journey of science and exploration, everyone is free to join this club! You have nothing to lose and everything to gain!

summary: The Office of Student Activities' mission is to enhance student experiences beyond the classroom by promoting career, social, and personal development. We also oversee the operations and management of Quintyne Hall and the Campus Center.

What we do:

The Office of Student Activities' mission is to enhance students’ experiences beyond the classroom by promoting career, social, and personal development. We office supports campus programming, student organizations, Fraternities & Sororities, support the Student Government Association, and oversee the operations and management of Quintyne Hall.

There are approximately 60 student clubs and organizations on campus overseen by the OSA. These consist of academic, club sports, cultural/religious, fraternities and sororities, performing arts, pre-professional organizations, recreational, social awareness, and special interest groups. Students can join clubs and organizations to take advantage of amazing networking and leadership opportunities, explore or confirm a career path, learn new skills, sharpen old skills, and develop life-long friendships.

All organizations and events are open to all students at Farmingdale State College at all times, allowing full participation in ALL events and activities

Club Recognition & Registration Process:

Fall Semester -

New Club Proposal Forms are accepted from April 1st to May 1st.

Returning Club Registration is open from June 1st to the first Friday in October. During this period clubs must meet the following requirements: submit a Re-Registration Form (portal renewal), all "Core 4" Officers complete Executive Board/RamCentral Training, Sexual Assault Prevention Training, and accept their position Terms & Conditions Agreements.

Spring Semester -

New Club Proposal Forms are accepted from November 1st to December 1st.

Returning Club Registration is open from December 1st to the first Friday in March. During this period clubs must meet the following requirements: submit a Re-Registration Form (portal renewal), all "Core 4" Officers complete Executive Board/RamCentral Training, Sexual Assault Prevention Training, and accept their position Terms & Conditions Agreements.

Office of Student Activities Semester Deadlines

What You'll Need to Propose a New Club:

4 current FSC students in good academic/social standing to serve as the President, Vice President, Treasurer, and Secretary, a Constitution detailing the purpose and mission of the club, and a Roster of 10 current FSC students who would be interested in joining the club if approved.

name: Panhellenic Association
summary: Promoting Service, Unity, Leadership, and Sisterhood throughout our three Sororities: ΣΔΤ, ΦΣΣ and ΔΦΕ.
description:
We, as Panhellenic women of Farmingdale State College, agree on and commit to:

• Uphold and demonstrate the Panhellenic spirit in thought, word and action through our chapters as well as individual members.

• Demonstrate ethical behavior and conduct ourselves in a manner consistent with the mission and values of the College Panhellenic, each inter/national organization and our university.

• Respectfully adhere to the Unanimous Agreements and all policies established by the National Panhellenic Conference.

• Avoid disparaging remarks about any fraternity or collegiate woman and refrain from discussing Panhellenic matters with nonmembers, in accordance with the dignity and good manners of fraternity women.

• Recognize friendly relations with all collegiate women, both fraternity members and nonmembers, realizing the importance of creating and building friendships.

• Plan recruitment events that provide opportunities for the greatest possible number of women to become fraternity members while protecting the rights and privileges of individuals and the chapters.

• Provide a safe, positive and enriching recruitment experience, understanding that membership is a social experience arrived at by mutual selection.

• Strive to be truthful, honorable, open and friendly to all potential new members during all recruitment events.

• Be respectful of the rights of every potential new member to make her own choices, including the right not to join the women’s fraternity community.

• Refrain from limiting a potential new member’s chances of becoming a member of the Panhellenic community by encouraging her to make a single intentional preference or to limit her choices.

name: Pre-Health Professions Club
summary: Farmingdale State College's Pre-Health Professions Club is a club organized by students interested in pursuing a career in the medical field. Our members will advance their knowledge & skill set through collaborations, to better the future of healthcare.
description: Farmingdale State College's Pre-Health Professions Club (PHPC) is a club for students looking to advance their knowledge and skill set to be better prepared for the following stages of their careers in healthcare. Pursuing a career in the medical field can be challenging, but it is always helpful to have others like you working toward our ultimate goal. We strive to create a community for students to maximize their full potential and become educated about careers in healthcare. As a community, we want to be a support group for those individuals who may be interested in entering the medical field. PHPC strives to create a diverse and inclusive environment to fulfill our ultimate goal of creating a brighter future in healthcare.

name: Pre-Law Society
summary: Are you interested in law school or expanding your legal knowledge? The Pre-Law Society at Farmingdale State College is the perfect place to explore the legal field. Join us for LSAT prep, mock trials, guest speakers, networking events, and more!
description:
The Pre-Law Society at Farmingdale State College is a student-led organization dedicated to preparing undergraduates for law school and careers in the legal field. Our mission is to create a supportive community where students can explore law through mock trial events, guest speakers, informational events and networking opportunities with attorneys, judges, and law schools. We'll also provide resources like LSAT study groups and a network of legal professionals to help members grow academically and professionally. Rooted in excellence, integrity, and community, the Society strives to empower future leaders who will use the law as a tool for justice and change.

Well known civil rights attorney Frederick K. Brewington spoke to the FSC Pre-Law Society in Spring 2024, inspiring our members with the reminder that striving for excellence is what we do. This is your sign to join the Pre-Law Society and be part of a community dedicated to growth, leadership, and impact.

name: Pre-Physical Therapy Club

description:
The Pre-Physical Therapy Club is designed to support aspiring DPT and PTA students in their journey towards preparing for physical therapy programs. Our mission is to establish a dedicated support network that cultivates a nurturing environment where students can exchange experiences, engage in collaborative study sessions, and extend emotional support to one another, especially through the rigorous application process.

Additionally, we are committed to reinforcing professional guidance by actively partnering with advisors and faculty members who bring expertise in academic and career domains. The club strives to create a community where students can maximize their potential and become well-informed about the physical therapy career.

By fostering a supportive and collaborative atmosphere, the Pre-Physical Therapy Club aims to empower students to achieve their academic and career goals in physical therapy, ensuring they are well-prepared for the next stages of their careers. Whether you are a pre-physical therapy student or simply interested in the field, we welcome you to join our community and take advantage of the valuable resources and support we offer.

The club provides members with a supportive environment to strengthen the communication and interpersonal skills needed to succeed across a variety of industries and career paths.

Through interactive workshops, role-play activities, sales frameworks, guest speakers, networking events, and career-focused programming, members gain practical experience in pitching ideas, conducting discovery, communicating value, building professional relationships, interviewing, and presenting themselves with confidence.

The Professional Sales Club also helps students develop their personal brand and better understand how to translate their academic, professional, and extracurricular experiences into skills that employers value. Whether members are interested in pursuing a career in sales, marketing, business, entrepreneurship, or another professional field, the club provides opportunities to practice real-world skills, connect with peers and professionals, and become more confident and prepared for their future careers.

be streamed anywhere, on your computer, laptop, or mobile device through the Live365 app or website.

What makes us stand out? We’re not just a radio station, we’re a hub for campus life! You can expect:

description: Welcome to the Student Chapter of the Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers (SHPE) RAM Chapter at Farmingdale State College! We are thrilled to have you join our community dedicated to empowering and supporting Traditionally underrepresented students pursuing careers in engineering and related fields. One of the key objectives of our chapter is to foster a sense of belonging and community. We understand the unique challenges that Hispanic students may face in STEM fields, and we strive to create a safe and inclusive environment where you can connect with like-minded individuals, share experiences, and build lasting friendships. SHPE offers numerous opportunities for personal and professional growth. Through our chapter, you will gain access to a wide range of workshops, seminars, and conferences that focus on skill-building, leadership development, and career advancement. These events are designed to enhance your technical expertise, improve your communication skills, and expand your knowledge of industry trends and practices. At our SHPE RAM Chapter meetings, you can look forward to a dynamic and engaging experience that offers a multitude of opportunities for growth and exploration. We prioritize bringing in guest speakers who are industry professionals, researchers, and accomplished individuals from diverse backgrounds from within the campus or externally. These speakers share their insights, experiences, and expertise, providing valuable perspectives on various career paths and industries within engineering and related fields. By exposing yourself to different opportunities and industries, you will expand your horizons and gain a deeper understanding of the vast array of paths available to you. We are excited to embark on this journey with you, and we encourage you to take full advantage of the resources and opportunities available through our SHPE chapter. Together, let's build a thriving community of professionals in engineering and related fields, and shape a future where diversity and excellence go hand in hand. Welcome to SHPE RAM Chapter at Farmingdale State College!

name: Sociology Club
summary: Sociology Club is a student group that helps people learn about society and real life issues. The club gives students a safe place to talk, learn, and connect with others.
description: Sociology Club is a student group that creates a welcoming space for students who want to learn about society, culture, identity, inequality, institutions, and human behavior. The club encourages open conversation and simple discussions that help students understand real life issues. The club brings in guest speakers, holds workshops, plans trips, and takes part in community events. These activities help students connect classroom ideas to everyday life. The club also supports students who want to explore careers in fields like law, social work, psychology, public service, nonprofit work, and research. The club works with other groups on campus since many topics overlap. The goal is to help students feel supported and to build a strong community.

name: South Asian Student Association
summary: The South Asian Student Association (SASA) is an organization which aims to spread South Asian culture to Farmingdale State College by organizing events that involves both traditional and non-traditional cultural activities.
description: The South Asian Student Association (SASA) is an organization which aims to spread South Asian culture to Farmingdale State College (FSC) by organizing events that involves both traditional and non-traditional cultural activities. SASA likes to bring together the diverse cultures at FSC by co-sponsoring various activities. The club aims to foster unity and the spirit of South Asia. In order to understand South Asian culture, it is important to know what defines South Asian culture. The subcontinent of South Asia comprises of Afghanistan, India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan and Maldives. Between these countries there is a wider range of diversity in terms of cultural traditional and some overall similarities. Within South Asia the main religions consist of Hinduism, Islam, Sikhism and Buddhism. Each South Asian region had its own traits. It is through celebrating these difference and similarities that SASA encourage students of all ethnicities to help foster a wider understanding of South Asian culture.

name: Sport Management Club
summary: The Sport Management Club is for students who are interested in sports, especially their business aspect.
description:
Welcome to Sport Management Club page!

Our club is for students who are interested in sports, especially their business aspect. The club helps those students seeking a career in the sports industry to network and gain access to internships. In addition to regularly scheduled meetings where we talk about the latest sports news and brief members on available internships, we gain hands-on experience by visiting professional sporting venues. The club has given back to the community through the vehicle of sport, raising money and collecting sporting goods for Children's Sport Connection, a charity that helps underprivileged youths participate in athletics.

In the past, the club has been to the Barclays Center, James M. Shuart Stadium at Hofstra University, and Madison Square Garden. We have also had many guest speakers come to Farmingdale State College to share the experiences that they have had while working in the sports industry and impart to the club members any tips they have for breaking into the industry. Some of these speakers include Sandy Alderson (General Manager of the New York Mets), Adam Rubin (ESPN Baseball Journalist), Darren Meenan (Founder 7Line Clothing), and Erik Stover (Chief Operating Officer of the New York Cosmos).
